correctness.rationale: Every nonzero rank-one matrix over F_q[T] has monic content and two primitive vector factors, unique modulo precisely q-1 nonzero constants. Polynomial degree adds across factors and content equals the unique nonzero Smith invariant. Counting nonzero vectors by maximum coordinate degree yields V_k=(q^k-1)/(1-q^k z); stripping monic gcd yields P_k=(1-q z)V_k. Their product with the monic content series 1/(1-q w z), divided by q-1, proves the exact formal series. Leading pole orders yield the geometric content law with parameter q^(1-max(m,n)); exact coefficient extraction gives the height-shell formulas for both equal and unequal dimensions. Exhaustive independent polynomial-minor and gcd enumeration matched q=2,3 cases and published 2x2 unweighted counts.

originality.rationale: The direct 2026 published count covers only unweighted 2-by-2 determinant zero, explicitly credited; the bivariate Smith-content refinement with arbitrary rectangular sizes and geometric conditional limit is stronger in distinct dimensions and statistics and was not located in checked sources. A previously recorded degree joint law for factorizations of equal polynomial products is not a joint matrix-content enumeration. These negative searches are not uniqueness proofs; abstract height-zeta implication is disclosed as a residual risk.
residual_risks: A broader indexed or unindexed height-zeta theorem for rational points on Segre varieties may imply the exact rank-one content-height series; only abstract-level access was obtained to one plausible toric height source.
Published-record semantic search does not certify global novelty.
The unweighted 2x2 special case is already proved in the motivating paper and has deliberately not been claimed independently.

value.rationale: Smith content is a canonical invariant of rank-one polynomial matrices. The complete bivariate height-content series determines all finite content slices for unbounded matrix dimensions, a geometric limiting distribution with a dimension-dependent parameter, and a sharp square/rectangular height transition. These are natural refinements of a recent zero-determinant enumeration rather than arbitrary parameter instances; the 2x2 unweighted special case is explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. Generalization to higher rank is not asserted.
